entries.content:
You can now run CI for your Turborepo with one line of configuration.

      
{  "tasks": {    "lint": {      "tags": ["ci"]    }  }}

Use tags to make a task run in Vercel CI.

In Vercel's internal repositories, our wait time from 

git push
to "CI passed" is 2-6x shorter, dramatically improving our CI's ability to keep up with our coding agents.

To get started, prompt your agent in your repo:

Set up Vercel CI for this repository. Run `npx skills use vercel/ci@setup` and follow the skill's instructions to select initial tasks, configure Vercel CI, and open a pull request.

Each task marked with a 

ci
tag runs on every push. Vercel CI automatically takes care of:

  • Only running CI that is affected by your code changes

  • Task caching with Vercel Remote Cache

  • Installing dependencies once per run

  • Caching dependencies across code updates

To learn more:

entries.content:
Box Mount lets agents running in Vercel Sandbox read and write Box files through standard filesystem operations. It syncs a Box folder with a directory inside the sandbox. Unmount before you stop the sandbox, and everything the agent wrote is in Box after the sandbox is deleted.

The contract-review example uses AI Gateway to review a synthetic contract in Vercel Sandbox and save the review back to Box. The sync process and agent run as separate sandbox users, keeping the Box credentials separate from the agent's workspace.

Box Mount is in private preview. Request access from Box, then follow the Box Mount documentation to set it up in Vercel Sandbox.

entries.content:
Vercel Container Registry now supports up to 2 GB per compressed image layer, up from 500 MB, allowing larger layers to be pushed without splitting them. The total image size limit remains 15 GB.

The higher layer limit is useful for images with large toolchains or dependency sets, such as custom Vercel Sandbox environments for coding-agent evaluations.

With Docker and the Vercel CLI installed, run these commands from the directory containing your Dockerfile:

      
vercel linkvercel vcr login dockervercel vcr build docker . --push

Link your project, authenticate Docker, then build and push the image.

Read the Vercel Container Registry getting-started guide to build, push, and pull your first container image.

entries.content:
Today, we are introducing Virtual Models on AI Gateway.

Virtual Models are an abstraction of the model string and configurations your apps and developers use. With a single virtual model ID, you can change and update models, configure fallbacks and priority, and enforce Zero Data Retention centrally. The virtual model configuration applies wherever the ID is used.

Assign a virtual model ID to an agent task, and pass it as the model string wherever that task is called. You can then change the model and settings behind the virtual model ID in AI Gateway, and your apps and agents will pick up the new configuration automatically, without code changes or redeploys.

Copy link to headingNew models use the same virtual model ID

In the last 90 days, 125 new models from more than 10 labs became available on AI Gateway. That adds up to about 10 a week. AI Gateway already makes switching a one-line change. You call any of those models by ID, and AI Gateway routes each request to a healthy provider and can fall back to others when one fails.

That one line still lives in your code, so switching usually means a redeploy.

Virtual Models move model selection and configuration to AI Gateway. You create an ID for a task, like 

vmc/coding-agent
, and then configure the model and the settings it should use: 
      
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models create coding-agent \  --model anthropic/claude-opus-5.5 \  --config '{"speed":"fast","zeroDataRetention":true}'

You can then use that virtual model ID as the model string wherever the task runs:

      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'vmc/coding-agent',  prompt: 'Remove the deprecated API calls from this module.',});

For coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and others, connect them with 

vercel ai-gateway setup
, then select your virtual model in each harness's model picker or configuration.

When a different model is available, including one from another provider, edit the virtual model. Every app and agent that calls 

vmc/coding-agent
picks it up within a few minutes, with no code change or deployment needed: 
      
vercel ai-gateway virtual-models edit coding-agent --model openai/gpt-6.1-sol

Copy link to headingGive each task its own model

An agent task like support ticket triage can run hundreds of times an hour and needs to be cheap. Other tasks, like legal contract review, may only run a few times a day, but require a high level of reasoning.

You can now give each task a purpose-built virtual model, and easily evolve that model and configuration over time:

Settings such as fallbacks, Zero Data Retention, and tags stay with the virtual model when you switch models. Provider options apply per provider, so an Anthropic-specific setting stops applying when you point the virtual model at an OpenAI model. Review your provider options whenever you switch providers.

Before you switch a virtual model that serves production traffic, point a second one, like 

vmc/coding-agent-candidate
, at the new model and run your evals against it. If quality drops after the switch, point the original back at the previous model.

Copy link to headingGovern which models your team uses and how

Anyone on your team can call a virtual model, and team roles control who can make changes to them. Platform and security teams can centrally govern and test models and settings, while still easily giving teams access to new models as they are released.

Settings on a virtual model win over the same settings in a request, so callers can't override the provider order, fallbacks, or service tier you chose. For example, you can configure the fallback models for 

vmc/storefront-assistant
centrally, and every app using that virtual model ID will use the same failover configuration, even if a request specifies different fallbacks.

If a virtual model requires Zero Data Retention or providers that don't train on request data, those configurations are enforced even if a request explicitly sets 

zeroDataRetention
or 
disallowPromptTraining
to false.

Tags on a virtual model replace any tags sent with the request, so spend lands on the task no matter how each app tags its calls. The Virtual Models page shows requests, spend, and success rate for each task.

Copy link to headingGet started

Create a virtual model from your team dashboard or with the Vercel CLI.

Copy link to headingAbout AI Gateway

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and doesn't charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

Virtual Models work with every model type on AI Gateway, including image, video, speech, embedding, and realtime models, and with the AI SDK and the OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible APIs. See the Virtual Models documentation for every setting.

entries.title: Introducing Vercel CI
entries.summary: Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. entries.content:
Coding agents are opening more pull requests than ever, and each one waits on CI before anyone can review or merge it. Most CI systems run the entire workflow on every push, even a one-line change. The more your agents push, the more time you spend waiting on CI.

Today, we're announcing Vercel CI in Beta. It runs only the tasks affected by your code change, and spins up only the compute those checks need, the same way Fluid compute scales with your traffic.

At Vercel, our CI now keeps up with our coding agents. Time from 

git push
to "CI passed" is 2-6x faster than it was before.

Copy link to headingHow it works

Vercel CI uses Turborepo to understand your tasks and which ones depend on each other. It reads 

turbo.json
, so if you're already using Turborepo, there's no separate CI config to write.

If you're not on Turborepo yet, add 

turbo.json
and the 
turbo
package. It works in single-package repos too.

Then tag the tasks you want Vercel CI to run.

      
{  "tasks": {    "lint": {      "tags": ["ci"]    }  }}

    

"tags": ["ci"]
is all you need to get started. No workflow YAML to maintain, no drift between your CI config and 
turbo.json
, and Remote Cache is on by default.

When you or your agent push code, Vercel CI determines which tasks need to run based on the change. Tasks whose inputs haven't changed come from cache. The remaining tasks each run on their own machine, powered by Hive, Vercel's compute layer, and start as soon as their dependencies finish.

Vercel CI gives each task the compute it needs and nothing more.

Copy link to headingRunning your CI on Vercel

To get started, follow the documentation or prompt your agent from your repo:

Set up Vercel CI for this repository. Run `npx skills use vercel/ci@setup` and follow the skill's instructions to select initial tasks, configure Vercel CI, and open a pull request.

Once set up, you or your agent can watch and inspect CI through the Vercel dashboard, Vercel CLI, or Vercel MCP. When something fails, go straight to the failing task, see what's blocked behind it, and open its logs, or search across recent runs to see whether a test has been flaky all week.

      
vc ci ls # List CI runs for the repositoryvc ci inspect  # List tasks for a runvc ci logs  # Get logs for all tasks in a runvc ci logs  --task web#test --level=error # Get stderr for a specific taskvc ci grep "WARNING" # Search across run logs for a string

Vercel CI posts a check to your pull request on GitHub, so your existing branch protection rules can block merges on failure, the same way they do today.

Copy link to headingClosing the loop

Vercel CI has already completed nearly 8 million tasks across our own repositories and the private beta, and we're just getting started. We're working to keep shrinking the time between writing code and running it in production.

As we work toward general availability, we plan to add:

  • Advanced observability

  • A 

    vc ci
    CLI command for distributed execution before pushing code

  • More granular test selection

Vercel CI is available in Beta today on all plans. Read the docs and try it on your repository.

entries.content:
Paseo now supports running fx, Codex, Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi in the cloud with the Vercel Sandbox plugin.

You can now start an agent in Vercel Sandbox from Paseo on your laptop, then connect from your phone to control the same session, even when your laptop is closed. Stopping a sandbox saves your files and conversation history so you can pick up where you left off. Active processes stop with the sandbox.

Enter your Vercel AI Gateway key once during setup. The plugin reuses it for model requests across your sessions, keeping the key outside the sandbox.

To get started, enable plugins in Settings → Plugins in Paseo. Then install the plugin:

      
paseo plugin add vercel-labs/paseo-vercel-sandbox

Learn more in the Sandbox documentation, Paseo plugin listing, and the Paseo related projects documentation.

entries.content:
Particle-1 from Particle AI is now available on AI Gateway. It is post-trained on DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, with a focus on completing software engineering tasks using fewer tokens. Particle describes the gains as shorter reasoning, fewer rounds of trial and repair, and more focused exploration.

Use it for debugging, planning code changes, and breaking down multi-step engineering problems. Particle-1 has a 1M-token context window for working with code and extended task histories.

Set 

AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY
in your environment. Use 
particle/particle-1
as the model name: 
      
import { streamText } from 'ai';
const result = streamText({  model: 'particle/particle-1',  prompt: 'Suggest three fixes for a flaky API retry loop.'});
for await (const text of result.textStream) {  process.stdout.write(text);}

To use it in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and more, install the latest version of Vercel CLI and run setup:

      
npx vercel ai-gateway setup

Then select 

particle/particle-1
in the agent. See the coding agents guide for details.

Try Particle-1 in the model playground.

AI Gateway provides a unified API for calling models, tracking usage and cost, and configuring retries, failover, and performance optimizations for higher-than-provider uptime. It includes built-in custom reporting, Zero Data Retention support, budgets for API keys, routing rules, and more.

AI Gateway reflects provider pricing with no markup and does not charge a platform fee on inference, including on Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) requests.

You can view all language models available on AI Gateway.

entries.summary: Vercel CLI no longer requires an interactive terminal to enable Web Analytics or Observability Plus. Agents can now turn them on for your projects without asking you to run the commands yourself.To get started, run either command from a linked project directory:Teams must already be subscribed to Observability Plus to be able to enable it for a project.Update Vercel CLI to version 64.2.0 or later
entries.content:
Vercel CLI no longer requires an interactive terminal to enable Web Analytics or Observability Plus. Agents can now turn them on for your projects without asking you to run the commands yourself.

To get started, run either command from a linked project directory:

      
vercel project web-analytics enablevercel project observability enable

Enabling Web Analytics or Observability Plus

Teams must already be subscribed to Observability Plus to be able to enable it for a project.

Update Vercel CLI to version 64.2.0 or later and learn more in the Vercel CLI project documentation.

entries.content:
You can now use fx, our open-source coding agent harness, in T3 Code on web, desktop, and mobile.

T3 Code is an open-source control plane for coding agents, allowing you to add agents like fx as providers for your coding sessions. The built-in fx provider supports Supervised and Auto modes, along with the models and skills you already use with fx.

Get started by installing fx and setting up your model provider. Then download T3 Code and add fx from Settings > Providers > Add provider.

entries.content:
The Vercel Plugin is now available in OpenCode.

The plugin provides guidance on Vercel APIs and recommended patterns, with skills for AI SDK, Vercel Functions, Workflow, and more. It also includes specialist agents for deployment, performance optimization, and AI application design. Use 

/vercel:deploy
to deploy projects and 
/vercel:env
to manage environment variables.

The plugin requires OpenCode 2. If you’re using OpenCode 1, upgrade with 

opencode upgrade --major
.

To install the plugin, run:

      
opencode plugin add github:vercel/vercel-plugin

Install the Vercel Plugin in OpenCode 2.

Then run 

/mcps
in OpenCode, select vercel, and sign in. This connects the Vercel MCP server so OpenCode can access your Vercel projects, deployments, and logs.

Learn more in the Vercel Plugin documentation.
